Title & Date
April 19, 2021

Attendees
- President Trigg-Scales (present)
- Vice President Tunnicliffe (present)
- Mrs. Huerta (present)
- Ms. Merklinger (present)
- Mr. Rothstein (present)
- Superintendent Dr. Cascone and Business Administrator/Board Secretary Ms. Flowers
- Mrs. de Mendez (curriculum), student liaisons, and about 200 members of the public at the peak

Purpose & Objectives
A virtual regular meeting to act on minutes, policies, personnel, curriculum, and finance items. Public comment centered on proposed 2021-2022 cuts to library media specialist and middle school choral positions and on the pace of reopening.

Key Discussion Points
- Dr. Cascone: hybrid instruction resumed April 19 after a two-week quarantine; updates on elementary Fridays and the May 3 start would follow this week. Secondary cohorts will be compressed after two weeks of moderate regional COVID risk.
- Summer and support programs: a virtual after-school program for about 50 middle school English language learners, plus high school and middle school summer programs funded partly or fully by ESSER II. More summer programs ($400,000 to $500,000 in local and grant funds) are expected May 10.
- Policy (Mr. Rothstein): 127 policies remain after tonight's 22; workshops April 26, May 20, June 10, and June 14, with a searchable Strauss Esmay platform by June.
- Legislative (Vice President Tunnicliffe): New Jersey's federal testing waiver was granted; Start Strong replaces the NJSLA this spring.
- Negotiations: the board is bargaining with the WOAA, the WOEA, and two Local 68 units.
- A second preschool expansion grant window is expected around June or July; the district may add in-district sections to compete.
- Ms. Merklinger asked to postpone curriculum item 3 (Amistad professional development by Dr. Kalfani of Essex County College) to clarify how presenters were vetted; Mrs. de Mendez said the district's diversity, equity and access committee selected him.
- About 40 public speakers. Most opposed cutting two library media specialists (including Ms. Soto at Hazel, a Title I school), a Liberty choral position, and school secretaries while adding a director of diversity, equity and inclusion, citing higher state aid and about $8 million in expected federal funds. Others pressed for full-time school, combined secondary cohorts, live Fridays, and in-person board meetings.
- Dr. Cascone on the budget: $177 million proposed; about $9.4 million in increases and $5,735,000 in state aid at the 1.5% levy consensus left almost $2.1 million in cuts. Federal funds are too uncertain for the budget due to the county May 3 but could later restore positions. Using about $3.5 million in banked cap would mean a 4% to 5% levy increase. The new central office hire is one position, not three; the budget adds seven certificated positions.
- President Trigg-Scales said meetings stay virtual to keep participation high, and the board would discuss the staff raised tonight in executive session.
- Reopening: full elementary days would require moving the high school back to a 7:30 a.m. start; full in-person school is the goal for September. Graduation is planned as multiple on-site ceremonies.
- Board reports: Ms. Merklinger apologized to faculty for earlier remarks on Fridays, noted she cast the only no vote on the new administrative positions, and proposed a budget workshop. Dr. Cascone called virtual-only teachers a concept pending state guidance and federal funds.

Decisions Made
- Approved the closed meeting minutes of March 18 and 22 and public meeting minutes of March 18, 22, and 25 (motion by Vice President Tunnicliffe, second by Mrs. Huerta; 5-0 roll call).
- Approved Attachment 2 policies on second reading (motion by Mr. Rothstein, second by Vice President Tunnicliffe; 5-0 roll call).
- Approved personnel items 1-3, Attachments 3-5 (motion by Mrs. Huerta; second not clear in the transcript; 5-0 roll call).
- Approved curriculum and instruction items 1-6, Attachment 6, including the Confucius Classroom grant and the ESSER II summer program (motion by Mrs. Huerta, second by Vice President Tunnicliffe; roll call with no no votes, the Vice President's answer not clearly audible).
- Approved finance items A and B, Attachments 7-10, including an $80 donation (motion by Vice President Tunnicliffe, second by Mr. Rothstein; 5-0 roll call).
- Moved into executive session with no further public action (motion by Mrs. Huerta, second by Vice President Tunnicliffe; voice vote).

Action Items
- Send a community update on elementary Fridays and the May 3 start -- Dr. Cascone -- Later this week
- Discuss elementary recess with principals -- Dr. Cascone -- Not specified
- Bring remaining summer programs for adoption -- Administration -- May 10 board meeting
- Present the assessment and learning gap report -- Mrs. de Mendez -- May 10
- Complete a draft ESSER II grant application -- Mrs. de Mendez and team -- May
- Announce middle and high school summer program dates -- Administration -- Upcoming weeks
- Submit the 2021-2022 budget to the county -- Administration -- May 3
- Hold policy workshops -- Board -- April 26, May 20, June 10, June 14
- Email remaining questions to the administration -- Ms. Merklinger -- Not specified

Unresolved Issues
- The proposed library media specialist, choral, and secretary cuts, and whether the diversity director salary, banked cap, or federal funds will restore positions.
- Ms. Merklinger's budget workshop proposal was not acted on.
- Curriculum item 3 was not voted on separately despite the postponement request; it appears to have passed with the full slate (no minutes on file to confirm).
- Timing for combining secondary cohorts, live Friday instruction, and a full-time September plan.
- Return of board meetings to an in-person or hybrid format.

Next Steps
The board went into executive session after midnight with no public action to follow. Upcoming: the April 26 policy workshop, the May 3 budget submission and hybrid expansion, and the May 10 board meeting.

A regular public meeting to hear the student liaison and superintendent reports, the 2023-2024 audit presentation, and Board committee reports, and to act on personnel, curriculum, finance, reports, and the 2025-2026 district calendar.

- Mr. Stevenson congratulated the members elected in November and sworn in on January 6, 2025.
- Student liaison Nina Davis reported on the Chinese Club's Lunar New Year celebration, the 19th annual West Orange High School Color Guard Invitational with more than 25 color guards, the AB Salute Boys Step Team's win at the 18th annual Youth Step USA Brooklyn Borough Championship on January 19, and a Black History Month dinner and celebration on February 13 (tickets $15).
- Mr. Moore reported that the first phase of electrical upgrades for elementary air conditioning is complete at Washington, Kelly, and St. Cloud, that work will begin at Mount Pleasant, Gregory, Hazel, and Redwood, and that he may ask PTAs to support a donation campaign to help install window units.
- Robert Haag of Lerch, Vinci & Bliss LLP presented the 2023-2024 audit: unmodified (clean) opinions on the financial statements, internal controls, and the single audit of state and federal grants. The district ended the year about $3.8 million above the state's 2 percent surplus limit, which will support the 2025-2026 budget (compared with about $3.7 million the prior year). The capital reserve held about $5.2 million, of which $5 million is budgeted this year, and the maintenance reserve about $2 million. He cautioned the Board to keep fund balance stable because surplus is used to support each following year's budget.
- The audit's management report had six recommendations, all general comments rather than significant deficiencies or material weaknesses. In response to a Board question, Mr. Haag said three were repeats from the prior year: the treasurer's surety bond was below the state minimum for the budget's size; supplemental pension reports and payments for retroactive pay must be filed for each affected quarter; and the capital asset appraisal report must be delivered before the audit is issued. A corrective action plan was on the agenda.
- Dr. Bryant (curriculum) reported that October 2024 district-wide classroom visits identified focus areas for grades 6-8 math, with progress toward giving students more of the cognitive work and more chances to explain and discuss their learning; diagnostics were being given that week, February visits will focus on student discussion, and the curriculum committee will receive progress reports on math and the new ELA implementation.
- President Rock reported that Roosevelt Middle School Principal Lionel Hush received the West Orange Human Relations Commission's 2025 Educator Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Award, and that student liaison Nina Davis was also honored there.
- Public comment on agenda items: Adam Kramer (Moran Road) raised policy questions from the audit: total revenue of $250,333,242 with enrollment of 7,880 (about $35,357 per student); about $256 million in combined town, county, and school debt (about $21,000 per household); the top ten taxpayers' share falling from 7.11 percent in 2015 to 5.4 percent; and more than $400,000 in bad debt, mostly from school lunches.
- Public comment: Margarita Sainz Soto, a Redwood kindergarten parent, asked about the air conditioning timeline. Mr. Moore said Redwood needs electrical upgrades and transformers that take about a year to arrive (already ordered), so Redwood is expected in 2026; air conditioning this year is planned for Washington, Kelly, and St. Cloud; he had no temporary cooling plan yet but would assess one, noting the district has used shared spaces, portables, and fans before.
- President Rock responded on the budget: individual preliminary budget meetings with the administration are scheduled, the Board will balance needs against taxpayer impact, the Board has issued no new major debt during his tenure, pre-K has expanded without a referendum, and the electrical upgrades were funded through the capital reserve and state funding without new debt.
- Public comment: Catherine DeWalker (Stanford) asked about heat safety protocols; Mr. Moore said temperature thresholds and plans to move students are in place.
- Petitions and hearings: Mr. Kramer said the district lacks a culture of accountability for ninth grade math results and costs, comparing per-pupil cost with Caldwell-West Caldwell.
- Petitions and hearings: Rochelle (Mayfair Drive), a parent and member of the West Orange Hispanic Foundation, asked whether school staff can tell a judicial warrant from an administrative one and know building access and student-privacy rules, given the federal rollback of the policy limiting immigration enforcement at schools. Pamela Beardsley shared her family's experience of separation under immigration law and asked whether emergency contacts are current and whether discipline and truancy protocols minimize student contact with law enforcement.
- Mr. Moore responded that he had sent a letter to families that day; that the district met the prior Thursday with its attorneys, the West Orange Police Department, and principals; that it would protect student and family confidentiality while acting lawfully, with the board attorney, police, and state guidelines guiding any response; that emergency contacts were being verified; and that attendance follow-up continues as usual.

- Accepted the closed and public meeting minutes of December 16, 2024, January 6, 2025, and January 15, 2025 (motion by Mr. Stevenson, second by Vice President Ivker; 5-0 roll call).
- Approved personnel items A1-A4, including the retirements of Jennifer Marchesi, St. Cloud special education teacher, after 30 years, and Brano Micic, West Orange High School night-shift custodian, after 23 years (motion by Mr. Stevenson, second by Vice President Ivker; 5-0 roll call).
- Approved curriculum and instruction items B1-B6, including school business and field trip requests and professional development from Teacher Created Materials ($5,500) and Therapeutic Learning Connections (motion by Mr. Stevenson, second by Vice President Ivker; 5-0 roll call).
- Approved finance items C, special services items 1-6 and business office items 1-12, including the January 27, 2025 bills list of $26,532,837.10; the 2025 Board designations; acceptance of the 2023-2024 audit and approval of the audit corrective action plan; commitment letters to private preschool providers pending additional preschool expansion slots; donations from Ms. Vera ($100 each to Hazel and Washington) and David Mende ($1,000 to Washington for summer music school); and the 2023-2024 Health and Safety Evaluation of School Buildings (motion by Mr. Stevenson, second by Vice President Ivker; 5-0 roll call).
- Approved reports items D1-D3: the School Safety Data System report for September to December 2024, the HIB report, and affirmation of the superintendent's decisions in HIB incidents 002 through 008 (motion by Mr. Stevenson, second by Ms. Vera; 5-0 roll call).
- Approved the 2025-2026 district academic calendar (item E1) (motion by Dr. Bryant, second by Ms. Vera; 4-0 roll call, Mr. Stevenson abstaining).
- Adjourned at 7:25 p.m. with no executive session to follow (motion by Mr. Stevenson, second by Dr. Bryant; 5-0 voice vote).

- Complete electrical upgrades and air conditioning at the remaining elementary schools -- District administration -- Washington, Kelly, and St. Cloud this year; Redwood expected 2026

- Hold individual preliminary budget meetings with Board members -- Administration and Board -- 2025-2026 budget season
